extracted.intended_audience: DoD contracting officers, A-76 program managers, installation commanders, and acquisition personnel involved in competitive sourcing studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for planning, staffing, managing, and executing OMB A-76 competitive sourcing (commercial activity) studies within the Department of Defense, including acquisition strategy, PWS development, source selection, risk management, and post-award oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management structure for A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: A sound management structure is needed to support the A-76 study; senior management (including installation commander) involvement lends credibility and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses recommended formal structures (e.g., an 'A-76 Council' or an Integrated Product Team (IPT)). Given complexity, a management approach similar to major weapon systems (a 'quasi' program office) is preferable. Management must be able to meet timelines, resolve stakeholder conflicts, and develop an acquisition strategy to manage identifiable risk factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of a full-time A-76 program manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Installations should have a full-time program manager for A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The acquisition strategy should make the program manager the focus of effort from program onset. An A-76 program manager complements IPTs and helps avoid ineffective management that causes delays, budget overruns, and poor PWS development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing the study team (full-time vs collateral duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine options for assigning A-76 study team members on a full-time basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-time assignment helps meet timelines and focus efforts; opponents argue full-time staff may lose touch with the work being studied. To mitigate technical competence loss, team members should work closely with the activities under study. Beware conflicts of interest where staff answer to multiple bosses; consider compiling 'undesirable' personnel lists and scrubbing candidate lists with legal counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition strategy as the central document
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquisition strategy is the single most important document the A-76 team will put together and should set the framework for the sourcing decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It must be the team's focus from the outset. The acquisition strategy should address contract type choice, risk management, evaluation approaches, past performance consideration, and cost comparison methodology. Gaps in acquisition strategy detail were noted in lessons learned and surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of contract type based on requirements maturity and risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract type should be chosen early based on known requirements, maturity of cost analysis, and risk both parties assume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid defaulting to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) for all studies—FFP may be inappropriate where variable costs are high (e.g., food services). Consider Fixed-Price-Incentive-Firm, Fixed-Price Award-Fee, or cost-reimbursement contracts depending on uncertainty and cost knowledge. The contract type affects later need for contract changes and performance outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-fee contract use criteria and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using incentive or award-fee contracts, examine administrative costs and ensure FAR conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR-specified criteria include: (1) expected administrative costs of award-fee evaluations should not exceed expected benefits; (2) procedures must be established for conducting award-fee evaluations; (3) the agency must provide for periodic evaluation of contractor performance against an award-fee plan; (4) the Government's determination of award fee is unilateral and not subject to the Disputes Clause. The award amount must motivate excellence in quality, timeliness, technical ingenuity, and cost-effective management. Also weigh ongoing post-award administrative burden versus benefits of contractor responsiveness and continuous improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of past performance in source selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Past performance of private firms can be a key indicator of expected government service level; however, measuring past performance of Government organizations (current operations or MEO) under A-76 is problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the MEO has no prior performance data, contracting officers considering past performance should set grading criteria and normalize scores for firms without past performance data; apply same normalization when evaluating the MEO proposal. Do not dismiss past performance outright—use it to select a competitive firm to challenge the MEO where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Best Value principles rather than only price
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 allows evaluating private offers and the MEO in a 'best value' sense, but implementation currently emphasizes lowest price technically acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To achieve best value, capture cost and past performance data on Government activities and allow contracting officers discretion to award based on factors other than price (technical approaches, management plans, past performance). Recommendations include amending A-76 to permit awards on non-price conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'technical leveling' and protect proprietary information in MEO discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: During discussions with the MEO there is a risk of inadvertently revealing proprietary information or 'technically' leveling the playing field in favor of the MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers must tailor comments to the MEO appropriately to avoid doing anything that would advantage the MEO and invite protests from private firms. Maintain clear boundaries and communications protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) must reflect current scope and amount of work
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS is the most important task in an A-76 study and should reflect the scope and amount of work currently performed; adding work should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An inflated PWS can prompt protests and legal action, as contractors will bid on inflated work while the MEO is constructed around actual current work. Failure to construct an adequate PWS leads to unhappy customers, contract modifications, price escalation, and loss of projected savings. Contracting officer should act as a trusted advisor and be involved from the beginning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and validation of the PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: PWS verification is critical—use Activity Based Costing (ABC) and technical experts familiar with current Government operations to validate requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where ABC is not widely adopted, ensure technical experts review the PWS and that team members interact frequently with the activities studied. Use a modified work breakdown structure to map major sub-components and validate requirements as the team builds up to major components of the commercial activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'gold plating' requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Gold plating' (adding unnecessary requirements) poses a significant risk to the competitive sourcing team and contracting officer and can open the command to protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requirements reflect necessary scope; validate against current operations and avoid adding work that benefits the command but is outside the existing activity scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing the Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB) and SSAC without conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: The contracting officer should ensure SSEB and SSAC staffing does not impose conflicts of interest or legal violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure evaluators are beyond reproach; failure to identify conflicts may require restarting acquisitions and can allow improper access to proposals or unfair aid to MEO development. Compile a conflicts-of-interest database listing employees forbidden from participating, and use legal counsel to scrub desirable/undesirable lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and management throughout the A-76 life cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and manage risks (e.g., employee reactions, PWS issues, timelines, stakeholder conflicts, contract bundling effects) consistently across A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk management is inconsistently applied; teams must proactively identify a full spectrum of risks, not only employee reaction. Key risk area noted: the PWS. Develop mitigation steps (e.g., WBS validation, PWS verification) and consider impacts such as contract bundling excluding small firms. Use acquisition strategy and IPTs to manage risks and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance contract bundling with small business and mandatory source policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract bundling/omnibus contracts can maximize economies of scale but risk excluding small or disadvantaged firms, and may conflict with policy (FAR 19.201, JWOD, FPI precedence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers must balance bundling benefits with statutory obligations to provide maximum practicable opportunities to small, HUBZone, small disadvantaged, and women-owned small businesses. Consider issuing a draft solicitation for industry comment to assess participation by mandatory sources and explore subcontracting strategies (primary with diversified subcontractors) to include small firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage solicitation-phase risks: communications and adherence to procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Risks during solicitation include improper communications with offerors (contractors and MEO) and source selection procedures that do not mirror solicitation standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle communications per standard procurement practices and tailor comments to MEO to prevent leveling. Ensure source selection procedures strictly follow evaluation criteria stated in the solicitation to avoid protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict adherence to cost comparison methodology in award phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest award-phase risk is improper cost comparison; contracting officers should strictly adhere to OMB A-76 cost comparison steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases exist where improper cost estimates led to reversed awards. Accurate, documented cost comparisons are essential to withstand appeals and prevent contractor claims for compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control post-award scope changes and unauthorized directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-award, manage the risk of unauthorized changes to contract scope and unauthorized directions by Marines or other personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure only the contracting officer is authorized to change contract scope. Work with COTRs and Marine commands to instruct personnel on appropriate interaction with contractors and the limits of authority to prevent unauthorized work requests and resultant contract risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage risk of protests by following solicitation evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of protests is managed by following procedures established in the solicitation; deviations from stated evaluation criteria lead to protests and overturned awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the evaluation criteria as written; document evaluations and decisions. Deviations are a principal cause of protests and can invalidate awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and maintain centralized lessons-learned and best-practices database
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD should maintain a centralized Internet-accessible database (under USD(A&T) Acquisition Web) of lessons learned and best practices from completed A-76 studies, with services required to submit input after each study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary focus should be study management, contracting issues, lessons learned, and best practices for developing PWS. A centralized repository would mitigate dispersed and incomplete information across Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend OMB A-76 to capture government cost and past performance data
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify OMB Circular A-76 to include instructions for capturing cost and past performance data on Government organizations under study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect similar data on Government activities as for commercial firms to support 'best value' determinations. Amendments should allow incorporating past performance, technical approaches, and management plans into evaluation criteria so contracting officers can award based on overall value, not just price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish waiver procedures for installation commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Create waiver procedures allowing installation commanders to protect commercial activities they deem mission critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers would let installation commanders tailor competitive sourcing studies to local conditions and protect mission-critical activities from mandatory competition, increasing the likelihood of delivering required services and cost savings.
